the black hole masses estimated from the reverberation-mapping-based BLR size for extremely radio-lou AGNs should be corrected by the factor $0.68/(1+0.68)$ to obtain the correct values.

for radio-quiet AGNs, both the optical luminosity and the emission line luminosity are good tracers of the photoionizing luminosities, while for extremely radio-lou d AGNs, the optical continuum is dominated by the jet and thus the optical emission line should be a better indicator of the photoionization luminosity.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we should use the $R-L_\nu$ relation derived with the same emission line to estimate the black hole mass of AGN.
the optical luminosity may be not a good indicator of ionizing luminosities for blazar-type  AGNs.
